page: OVHcloud r3-512 is a memory-optimized cloud server built for data-intensive processing and large memory requirements. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.3 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. It is provisioned with 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per core memory-to-CPU ratio. Hardware storage consists of a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include a hardware GPU accelerator.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core and throughput performance alongside top-tier memory processing capabilities. The instance scored 194,535.72 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 20,691.0 in Geekbench multi-core, reflecting top-decile execution across massive parallel workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 813.47 GB/sec, while PassMark registered a memory score of 3,020.92 and a CPU score of 94,314.31. In memory-centric tests, Redis SET throughput reached 134.58 million operations per second, supported by read-only memory bandwidth measuring 8,439.52 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 296.1 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks.

Single-threaded performance presents a noticeable contrast to its parallel throughput. The server scored 1,902.0 in single-core Geekbench and recorded average marks in single-threaded gzip compression at 29.15 GB/sec. Additionally, while the 400 GB local NVMe SSD provides low-latency local scratch space, it is relatively modest compared to the extensive 512 GB RAM footprint. From an efficiency perspective, the provision of 64 fully dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading ensures predictable execution times and eliminates noisy neighbor contention across memory and compute lanes.

OVHcloud r3-512 is well-suited for distributed in-memory databases such as Redis or Memcached, large-scale ETL pipelines, intermediate caching tiers, Clang-based compilation farms, and parallelized data science jobs. Workloads demanding strict single-thread low latency or massive local physical storage are better addressed by compute-optimized or high-density storage configurations.
